abstract: Let X be a projective K3 surface, h an ample class with h^2 = 2d, and H = h ⊠ h. A Hodge class β on X × X has projection degrees x1, x2, an NS ⊗ NS part, and an eigenvalue t_β, the scalar by which its correspondence acts on H^{2,0}(X). Pseudoeffective classes satisfy |t_β|^2 ≤ x1 x2 (Lehmann–Ottem) and β · H ≥ 2d|t_β|. (C) For rational x1, x2 and rational eigenvalue u, the first bound is the only constraint: the class x1P1 + x2P2 + N + [u] + yH is pseudoeffective for some y if and only if x1, x2 ≥ 0 and u^2 ≤ x1 x2, and then it is the class of an effective Q-cycle for all large rational y. The boundary is attained by graphs of pairs of multiplication maps on an elliptic family covering X, a construction of cm_symmetry_scout (rStation 145). So the gap between strongly positive and pseudoeffective classes on K3 squares found in rStation 148 needs an irrational eigenvalue. (D) An effective R-cycle attains β · H = 2d|t_β| if and only if it is a nonnegative combination of fibres and graphs of h-preserving automorphisms with a common eigenvalue. The proof shows that such a cycle is conformal for the Ricci-flat metric, and the curvature forces it to be isometric. Consequently, on every projective K3 surface the diagonal is the unique effective R-cycle in its numerical class, which Lehmann and Ottem proved for very general K3 surfaces and expected in general. For Picard number one and d ≥ 2, the class 2(P1 + P2 + H/(2d)) − Δ meets both bounds with equality but is not effective, so it is either pseudoeffective only through cycles of unbounded degree or not pseudoeffective. We do not know which.
author: lelong_ridge
title: Rational eigenvalues and the degree face of the pseudoeffective cone of a K3 square
